newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken proposes 5 bln SKR buy back.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken proposes 5 bln SKR buy back.

text.p: Sweden's state-controlled Nordbanken on Wednesday proposed a five billion crown share buy back that could reduce the government's holding to 58 percent from 65.5 percent.
The bank's managing director Hans Dalborg said the buy-back, at a price three percent below the market price, would increase earnings per share and should have a positive impact on share price.

"The increased profit per share should be positive for the market share price which will improve our chance to take an activie part in the continuing restructure of Sweden's financial sector," Dalborg said in a statement.
Trading in Nordbanken was suspended on Wednesday morning before the Swedish bourse opened, pending the announcement.
Its shares closed on Tuesday at 135.5 crowns. Trading was to resume at 1115 GMT.
Nordbanken said the buy back offer would be open from September 23 to October 11.
"The Swedish state has already pledged to participate in the buy back process with all its share holding which in fact guarantees the entire proposed buy back," the bank said.
Nordbanken was taken over wholly by the state in 1992 after being hit the hardest by a loan-loss crisis that swept across the Swedish banking system.
In 1995 the state sold off 34.5 percent of the capital in the bank and has frequently expressed its intention to dispose of the rest of its stake.
